transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-02-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Morales (Redwood SRE Eng), Maya Singh (Acme SRE Lead), Liam O'Connor (Acme CTO), Priya Rao (Acme Platform Eng)
Meeting type: Incident postmortem / follow-up

Summary:
Brief sync to review the P1 incident from 2025-02-10 that impacted Acme's customer checkout chat assistant. Discussed timeline, root cause (KV cache eviction + autoscaler race), mitigations applied (rate limiting, shorter TTLs, temporary routing to smaller models), follow-on reliability improvements, and commercial implications (credit/short-term capacity).

Topics:
- Incident timeline and logs
- Root cause analysis: KV cache eviction under burst + autoscaler mis-scheduling
- Short-term mitigations already applied
- Longer-term reliability work: redundant cache, proactive throttling, autoscaler fixes, canary rollouts
- Next steps, benchmarks, docs to share

Transcript: (timestamps approximate; transcription imperfect in places)
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey all, thanks for joining. We'll run about 60 to 75 minutes-ish, start with the timeline. Maya do you want to kick off with what you saw on the customer side?
[00:15] Maya Singh: Yeah um thanks Alex. So on Feb 10 around 14:12 UTC we saw the chat assistant latency spike and then about 14:18 errors started to cascade into 504s, uh checkout flows slowed. We collected request ids, I'll paste them after.
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: And just to add - this was hitting peak traffic from a marketing drop so traffic was roughly 3x normal. We had some retries from the client too.
[00:45] Samira Patel: Got it. We pulled Redwood logs and what we saw was a KV cache eviction sequence that increased cold starts for the small shard group and the autoscaler concurrently removed a pod due to a mis-evaluated health metric. There's a race where cache miss combined with pod removal causes tokens to spike.
[01:05] Diego Morales: to be clear, the autoscaler evaluated a node as underutilized — because the metric aggregator had a 30s stale window — and then scaled down. That plus the large prefix cache miss meant multiple requests triggered weight load, and latency spiked. We should apologize again because that shouldn't coincide.
[01:30] Maya Singh: Yeah that matches what we saw. We lost about 8% of chat requests and about 12% had >3s extra latency which broke the front-end guardrails.
[01:48] Priya Rao: quick question, was this on the hosted pool or Dedicated?
[01:52] Samira Patel: This happened on Hosted. Your org is on hosted with auto-scaling across n1 & n2 hardware tiers; the mis-schedule was in the region pool.
[02:05] Liam O'Connor: Could we have run this on Dedicated? We were considering Dedicated but worried about cost.
[02:10] Alex Chen: Yeah we discussed Dedicated in the past. Dedicated would give more predictable capacity, but not a silver bullet for autoscaler logic. In this case the root cause is policy and the KV cache behavior. We recommended short-term mitigations which we did apply.
[02:30] Maya Singh: What were the short-term mitigations? We saw some routing changes around 14:25.
[02:35] Samira Patel: Right — at 14:26 we applied a routing rule to failover to a smaller, lower-latency model variant that had warm cache, we also tightened rate limiting on the chat route and reduced TTLs for prefix cache to avoid large bulk evictions. We also temporarily disabled the automatic downscale window for the affected pool.
[02:58] Diego Morales: note: temp changes were a manual override; we still need engineering fixes so this doesn't require manual intervention next time.
[03:10] Liam O'Connor: There's also the question of revisions and audits. We had SLA triggers; we'd like the postmortem doc for compliance.
[03:20] Alex Chen: We'll send a consolidated postmortem with timeline, logs, and remediation plan. Samira will include the log snapshots and Diego will include perf traces.
[03:32] Priya Rao: can you include the KMS/HSM notes? Our security team asked about e2e.
[03:36] Samira Patel: Yes, we'll include a pointer to the KMS integration docs and SOC2 artifacts.
[03:42] Maya Singh: Another items — there were a handful of request ids that showed a model mismatch error where the client requested function calling. The transcription or .... uh something in the model output changed shape and the front-end couldn't parse.
[03:58] Samira Patel: we'll look into the function-calling edgecases; could be a model variant mismatch or an inference runtime path that omitted the schema enforcement.
[04:15] Diego Morales: jumping into RCA detail — root cause appears to be a sequence of: 1) Traffic spike due to marketing, 2) Cache eviction caused by TTL and burst, 3) Autoscaler scaled down a node due to stale metric window, 4) Warmup sequence for model caused token compute spiky CPU and memory pressure, 5) transient errors propagated to client.
[04:40] Maya Singh: Are we confident it's not an underlying infra network glitch? We saw a few packet retransmits.
[04:47] Diego Morales: we checked infra metrics — no region-wide network event. Packet retransmits were local to the pod during heavy GC cycles. Root cause still the combined load.
[05:05] Liam O'Connor: Ok clear. On mitigations — what's the recommended permanent fix?
[05:10] Samira Patel: Short list: (a) reduce default TTL for prefix/kvcache; (b) implement proactive pre-warming for anticipated campaign traffic; (c) change autoscaler metric to use a shorter freshness window and include pending queue size; (d) add redundancy for cache (local + regional fallback); (e) refine routing policies to avoid mass failovers to identical shard groups.
[05:40] Priya Rao: pre-warming — is that something we do or Redwood does?
[05:44] Alex Chen: We can offer an assisted pre-warm as part of a pilot. For Dedicated we can also set reserved capacity during the campaign window. Samira/Diego can run a bench for your traffic pattern.
[05:58] Maya Singh: We'd like a bench that simulates our marketing bursts — 3x baseline for 20 mins, ramp up 5 mins.
[06:05] Diego Morales: noted. We'll simulate 5k concurrent chat reps and capture KV cache hit/miss, CPU/mem, and token throughputs.
[06:20] Liam O'Connor: On the commercial side — we had about 2 hours of degraded UX; what's the remediation on billing/credits?
[06:28] Alex Chen: We'll follow Redwood policy for P1s — we can propose a credit equivalent and also offer reduced pricing for a trial Dedicated window. I'll prepare options in the follow-up doc.
[06:40] Priya Rao: Please make sure that the SSO/SSO token exchange for our logs access remains intact. Last time we had issues with role-based access to the logs portal.
[06:50] Samira Patel: We'll ensure the right IAM links are included and I'll add steps so your team can pull logs without role problems.
[07:02] Maya Singh: Anything about rate limit tuning? We saw retries stack and that amplified the issue.
[07:07] Samira Patel: On the short-term we dropped client retry limit and implemented a 100ms jitter backoff; long-term we'll use client-side throttling guidance in the integration doc.
[07:22] Liam O'Connor: Are there any open vulnerabilities or compliance concerns from this incident?
[07:28] Alex Chen: No data exfiltration; logs show errors but no PII leak. We'll include that in the postmortem.
[07:36] Priya Rao: Great. For the longer-term reliability roadmap, can Redwood commit to the autoscaler metric change timeline?
[07:43] Diego Morales: We can commit to a patch in two sprints for the autoscaler metric window and a more thorough rollout plan for the redundancy work over the next quarter. We'll prioritize immediately.
[07:58] Maya Singh: ok timeline sounds reasonable.
[08:02] Samira Patel: I'll also add a canary rollout plan for model variants so warmup doesn't hit production. We can add a weighted canary with health checks that block downscale if warmup is in progress.
[08:18] Liam O'Connor: About canaries — what instrumentation will you provide so we can see early warning signs?
[08:24] Diego Morales: We'll provide per-route tracing and a token-level latency histogram in Console; also a pre-defined alert for cache hit ratio dropping below threshold.
[08:36] Alex Chen: we'll include dashboard links and a guide for alerts.
[08:42] Maya Singh: One more ask — can you capture the exact sequence of API calls that failed so our devs can reproduce?
[08:48] Samira Patel: Yes, Samira will attach a set of sample request ids and the proxied request/response traces.
[08:56] Priya Rao: Any mention of competitor options? Our security team asked because they evaluate alternatives.
[09:02] Alex Chen: Some customers look at Anthropic and OpenAI but those are more model-sourcing than managed inference policy. On-prem solutions can be more predictable but require ops. We'll include a short comparison table in the follow-up.
[09:18] Liam O'Connor: Ok thanks. Shall we recap next steps?
[09:22] Alex Chen: Yes. Recap: Redwood to send postmortem doc with timeline/logs/mitigations, run benchmark on staging Dedicated simulating the campaign, propose commercial remedial credits and trial. Customer to share exact request ids and endpoints.
[09:38] Maya Singh: I'll send request ids and a short impact statement by Feb 17.
[09:44] Diego Morales: we'll aim to run bench and post results by Feb 21.
[09:50] Samira Patel: I'll produce the postmortem + include SOC2/KMS docs by Feb 18.
[09:56] Alex Chen: I'll draft the pricing options and SOW for a trial Dedicated window by Feb 20.
[10:05] Liam O'Connor: Good. Anything else?
[10:08] Priya Rao: No, thanks everyone.
[10:10] Alex Chen: Great — we'll follow up in the thread and schedule the 2-week checkin. Thanks all.

Notes on transcription quality: speaker overlap in sections 02:30-04:00; some proper nouns (k-v cache, SLO) may be mis-capitalized or hyphenated. There are a few stutters and filler words left to keep transcript authenticity.
